model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the mean effect sizes, with error bars indicating variability, for six different multilingual language models—mBERT-L₂, XLM-L₂, mBERT-R₂, XLM-R₂, mBERT-B₂, and XLM-B₂—across nine linguistic categories: IE-Baltic, IE-Germanic, IE-Indic, IE-Romance, IE-Slavic family, IE-other, Isolate, Semitic, and Uralic. The horizontal axis lists these linguistic categories in alphabetical order, while the vertical axis, labeled “effect,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 30, with tick marks at intervals of 10. Each linguistic category is represented by a group of six bars, one for each model, colored as follows: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light pink), and XLM-B₂ (dark red). Within each group, the bars are arranged in the order specified by the legend, and their heights correspond to the mean effect values for that model in that language family. For example, in the IE-Indic category, the tallest bar is XLM-B₂ (dark red), reaching approximately 23, while the shortest bar is mBERT-L₂ (light blue), at approximately 1. In the Semitic category, the tallest bar is XLM-B₂ (dark red), reaching approximately 20, while mBERT-R₂ (dark green) is the shortest, at approximately -2. In the Uralic category, all bars are very short, with values near zero, and in the Isolate category, all bars are also near zero. The chart does not show any explicit sorting of categories by effect size, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their color coding and error bars.
